φαγοσ.def: from φάγω (G5315); a glutton. KJV: gluttonous.

φαγω.def: a primary verb (used as an alternate of ἐσθίω (G2068) in certain tenses); to eat (literally or figuratively). KJV: eat, meat.

φαινω.def: prolongation for the base of φῶς (G5457); to lighten (shine), i.e. show (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative). KJV: appear, seem, be seen, shine, X think.

φαλεκ.def: of Hebrew origin (H6389); Phalek (i.e. Peleg), a patriarch. KJV: Phalec.

φανεροσ.def: from φαίνω (G5316); shining, i.e. apparent (literally or figuratively); neuter (as adverb) publicly, externally. KJV: abroad, + appear, known, manifest, open (+ -ly), outward (+ -ly).

φανεροω.def: from φανερός (G5318); to render apparent (literally or figuratively). KJV: appear, manifestly declare, (make) manifest (forth), shew (self).

φανερωσ.def: adverb from φανερός (G5318); plainly, i.e. clearly or publicly. KJV: evidently, openly.

φανερωσισ.def: from φανερόω (G5319); exhibition, i.e. (figuratively) expression, (by extension) a bestowment. KJV: manifestation.

φανοσ.def: from φαίνω (G5316); a lightener, i.e. light; lantern. KJV: lantern.

φανουηλ.def: of Hebrew origin (H6439); Phanuel (i.e. Penuel), an Israelite. KJV: Phanuel.

φανταζω.def: from a derivative of φαίνω (G5316); to make apparent, i.e. (passively) to appear (neuter participle as noun, a spectacle). KJV: sight.

φαντασια.def: from a derivative of φαντάζω (G5324); (properly abstract) a (vain) show ("fantasy"). KJV: pomp.

φαντασμα.def: from φαντάζω (G5324); (properly concrete) a (mere) show ("phantasm"), i.e. spectre. KJV: spirit.

φαραγξ.def: properly, strengthened from the base of πέραν (G4008) or rather of ῥήγνυμι (G4486); a gap or chasm, i.e. ravine (winter-torrent). KJV: valley.

φαραω.def: of foreign origin (H6547); Pharao (i.e. Pharoh), an Egyptian king. KJV: Pharaoh.

φαρεσ.def: of Hebrew origin (H6557); Phares (i.e. Perets), an Israelite. KJV: Phares.

φαρισαιοσ.def: of Hebrew origin (compare H6567); a separatist, i.e. exclusively religious; a Pharisean, i.e. Jewish sectary. KJV: Pharisee.

φαρμακεια.def: from φαρμακεύς (G5332); medication ("pharmacy"), i.e. (by extension) magic (literally or figuratively). KJV: sorcery, witchcraft.

φαρμακευσ.def: from φάρμακον (a drug, i.e. spell-giving potion); a druggist ("pharmacist") or poisoner, i.e. (by extension) a magician. KJV: sorcerer.

φασισ.def: from φημί (G5346) (not the same as "phase", which is from φαίνω (G5316)); a saying, i.e. report. KJV: tidings.

φασκω.def: prolongation from the same as φημί (G5346); to assert. KJV: affirm, profess, say.

φατνη.def: from πατέομαι (to eat); a crib (for fodder). KJV: manager, stall.

φαυλοσ.def: apparently a primary word; "foul" or "flawy", i.e. (figuratively) wicked. KJV: evil.

φεγγοσ.def: probably akin to the base of φῶς (G5457) (compare φθέγγομαι (G5350)); brilliancy. KJV: light.

φειδομαι.def: of uncertain affinity; to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently. KJV: forbear, spare.

φειδομενωσ.def: adverb from participle of φείδομαι (G5339); abstemiously, i.e. stingily. KJV: sparingly.

φελονησ.def: by transposition for a derivative probably of φαίνω (G5316) (as showing outside the other garments); a mantle (surtout). KJV: cloke.

φερω.def: a primary verb (for which other, and apparently not cognate ones are used in certain tenses only; namely, οἴω; and ἐνέγκω; to "bear" or carry (in a very wide application, literally and figuratively, as follows). KJV: be, bear, bring (forth), carry, come, + let her drive, be driven, endure, go on, lay, lead, move, reach, rushing, uphold.

φευγω.def: apparently a primary verb; to run away (literally or figuratively); by implication, to shun; by analogy, to vanish. KJV: escape, flee (away).

φηλιξ.def: of Latin origin; happy; Phelix (i.e. Felix), a Roman. KJV: Felix.

φημη.def: from φημί (G5346); a saying, i.e. rumor ("fame"). KJV: fame.

φημι.def: properly, the same as the base of φῶς (G5457) and φαίνω (G5316); to show or make known one's thoughts, i.e. speak or say. KJV: affirm, say.

φηστοσ.def: of Latin derivation; festal; Phestus (i.e. Festus), a Roman. KJV: Festus.

φθανω.def: apparently a primary verb; to be beforehand, i.e. anticipate or precede; by extension, to have arrived at. KJV: (already) attain, come, prevent.

φθαρτοσ.def: from φθείρω (G5351); decayed, i.e. (by implication) perishable. KJV: corruptible.

φθεγγομαι.def: probably akin to φέγγος (G5338) and thus to φημί (G5346); to utter a clear sound, i.e. (generally) to proclaim. KJV: speak.

φθειρω.def: probably strengthened from φθίω (to pine or waste); properly, to shrivel or wither, i.e. to spoil (by any process) or (generally) to ruin (especially figuratively, by moral influences, to deprave). KJV: corrupt (self), defile, destroy.

φθινοπωρινοσ.def: from derivative of φθίνω (to wane; akin to the base of φθείρω (G5351)) and ὀπώρα (G3703) (meaning late autumn); autumnal (as stripped of leaves). KJV: whose fruit withereth.

φθογγοσ.def: from φθέγγομαι (G5350); utterance, i.e. a musical note (vocal or instrumental). KJV: sound.

φθονεω.def: from φθόνος (G5355); to be jealous of. KJV: envy.

φθονοσ.def: probably akin to the base of φθείρω (G5351); ill-will (as detraction), i.e. jealousy (spite). KJV: envy.

φθορα.def: from φθείρω (G5351); decay, i.e. ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or figuratively). KJV: corruption, destroy, perish.

φιαλη.def: of uncertain affinity; a broad shallow cup ("phial"). KJV: vial.

φιλαγαθοσ.def: from φίλος (G5384) and ἀγαθός (G18); fond to good, i.e. a promoter of virtue. KJV: love of good men.

φιλαδελφεια.def: from Φιλάδελφος (the same as φιλάδελφος (G5361)), a king of Pergamos; Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor. KJV: Philadelphia.

φιλαδελφια.def: from φιλάδελφος (G5361); fraternal affection. KJV: brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren.

φιλαδελφοσ.def: from φίλος (G5384) and ἀδελφός (G80); fond of brethren, i.e. fraternal. KJV: love as brethren.

φιλανδροσ.def: from φίλος (G5384) and ἀνήρ (G435); fond of man, i.e. affectionate as a wife. KJV: love their husbands.

φιλανθρωπια.def: from the same as φιλανθρώπως (G5364); fondness of mankind, i.e. benevolence ("philanthropy"). KJV: kindness, love towards man.

φιλανθρωπωσ.def: adverb from a compound of φίλος (G5384) and ἄνθρωπος (G444); fondly to man ("philanthropically"), i.e. humanely. KJV: courteously.

φιλαργυρια.def: from φιλάργυρος (G5366); avarice. KJV: love of money.

φιλαργυροσ.def: from φίλος (G5384) and ἄργυρος (G696); fond of silver (money), i.e. avaricious. KJV: covetous.

φιλαυτοσ.def: from φίλος (G5384) and αὐτός (G846); fond of self, i.e. selfish. KJV: lover of own self.

φιλεω.def: from φίλος (G5384); to be a friend to (fond of (an individual or an object)), i.e. have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of sentiment or feeling; while ἀγαπάω (G25) is wider, embracing especially the judgment and the deliberate assent of the will as a matter of principle, duty and propriety: the two thus stand related very much as θέλω (G2309) and βούλομαι (G1014), or as θυμός (G2372) and νοῦς (G3563) respectively; the former being chiefly of the heart and the latter of the head); specially, to kiss (as a mark of tenderness). KJV: kiss, love.

φιληδονοσ.def: from φίλος (G5384) and ἡδονή (G2237); fond of pleasure, i.e. voluptuous. KJV: lover of pleasure.

φιλημα.def: from φιλέω (G5368); a kiss. KJV: kiss.

φιλημων.def: from φιλέω (G5368); friendly; Philemon, a Christian. KJV: Philemon.

φιλητοσ.def: from φιλέω (G5368); amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity. KJV: Philetus.

φιλιππησιοσ.def: from Φίλιπποι (G5375); a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. native of Philippi. KJV: Philippian.

φιλιπποι.def: plural of Φίλιππος (G5376); Philippi, a place in Macedonia. KJV: Philippi.

φιλιπποσ.def: from φίλος (G5384) and ἵππος (G2462); fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites. KJV: Philip.

φιλοθεοσ.def: from φίλος (G5384) and θεός (G2316); fond of God, i.e. pious. KJV: lover of God.

φιλολογοσ.def: from φίλος (G5384) and λόγος (G3056); fond of words, i.e. talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian. KJV: Philologus.

φιλονεικια.def: from φιλόνεικος (G5380); quarrelsomeness, i.e. a dispute. KJV: strife.

φιλονεικοσ.def: from φίλος (G5384) and νεῖκος (a quarrel; probably akin to νῖκος (G3534)); fond of strife, i.e. disputatious. KJV: contentious.

φιλονεξια.def: from φιλόξενος (G5382); hospitableness. KJV: entertain stranger, hospitality.

φιλοξενοσ.def: from φίλος (G5384) and ξένος (G3581); fond of guests, i.e. hospitable. KJV: given to (lover of, use) hospitality.

φιλοπρωτευω.def: from a compound of φίλος (G5384) and πρῶτος (G4413); to be fond of being first, i.e. ambitious of distinction. KJV: love to have the preeminence.

φιλοσ.def: properly, dear, i.e. a friend; actively, fond, i.e. friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.). KJV: friend.

φιλοσοφια.def: from φιλόσοφος (G5386); "philosophy", i.e. (specially), Jewish sophistry. KJV: philosophy.

φιλοσοφοσ.def: from φίλος (G5384) and σοφός (G4680); fond of wise things, i.e. a "philosopher". KJV: philosopher.

φιλοστοργοσ.def: from φίλος (G5384) and στοργή (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children); fond of natural relatives, i.e. fraternal towards fellow Christian. KJV: kindly affectioned.

φιλοτεκνοσ.def: from φίλος (G5384) and τέκνον (G5043); fond of one's children, i.e. maternal. KJV: love their children.

φιλοτιμεομαι.def: middle voice from a compound of φίλος (G5384) and τιμή (G5092); to be fond of honor, i.e. emulous (eager or earnest to do something). KJV: labour, strive, study.

φιλοφρονωσ.def: adverb from φιλόφρων (G5391); with friendliness of mind, i.e. kindly. KJV: courteously.

φιλοφρων.def: from φίλος (G5384) and φρήν (G5424); friendly of mind, i.e. kind. KJV: courteous.

φιμοω.def: from φιμός (a muzzle); to muzzle. KJV: muzzle.

φλεγων.def: active participle of the base of φλόξ (G5395); blazing; Phlegon, a Christian. KJV: Phlegon.

φλογιζω.def: from φλόξ (G5395); to cause a blaze, i.e. ignite (figuratively, to inflame with passion). KJV: set on fire.

φλοξ.def: from a primary φλέγω (to "flash" or "flame"); a blaze. KJV: flame(-ing).

φλυαρεω.def: from φλύαρος (G5397); to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously. KJV: prate against.

φλυαροσ.def: from φλύω (to bubble); a garrulous person, i.e. prater. KJV: tattler.

φοβεροσ.def: from φόβος (G5401); frightful, i.e. (objectively) formidable. KJV: fearful, terrible.

φοβεω.def: from φόβος (G5401); to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy, to be in awe of, i.e. revere. KJV: be (+ sore) afraid, fear (exceedingly), reverence.

φοβητρον.def: neuter of a derivative of φοβέω (G5399); a frightening thing, i.e. terrific portent. KJV: fearful sight.

φοβοσ.def: from a primary φέβομαι (to be put in fear); alarm or fright. KJV: be afraid, + exceedingly, fear, terror.

φοιβη.def: feminine of φοῖβος (bright; probably akin to the base of φῶς (G5457)); Phœbe, a Christian woman. KJV: Phebe.

φοινικη.def: from φοῖνιξ (G5404); palm-country; Phœnice (or Phœnicia), a region of Palestine. KJV: Phenice, Phenicia.

φοινιξ.def: of uncertain derivation; a palm-tree. KJV: palm (tree).
probably the same as φοῖνιξ (G5404); Phœnix, a place in Crete. KJV: Phenice.

φονευσ.def: from φόνος (G5408); a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which ἀνθρωποκτόνος (G443) does not necessarily imply; while σικάριος (G4607) is a special term for a public bandit). KJV: murderer.

φονευω.def: from φονεύς (G5406); to be a murderer (of). KJV: kill, do murder, slay.

φονοσ.def: from an obsolete primary φένω (to slay); murder. KJV: murder, + be slain with, slaughter.

φορεω.def: from φόρος (G5411); to have a burden, i.e. (by analogy) to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment. KJV: bear, wear.

φορον.def: of Latin origin; a forum or market-place; only in comparative with Ἄππιος (G675); a station on the Appian road. KJV: forum.

φοροσ.def: from φέρω (G5342); a load (as borne), i.e. (figuratively) a tax (properly, an individual assessment on persons or property; whereas τέλος (G5056) is usually a general toll on goods or travel). KJV: tribute.

φορτιζω.def: from φόρτος (G5414); to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e. (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety). KJV: lade, by heavy laden.

φορτιον.def: diminutive of φόρτος (G5414); an invoice (as part of freight), i.e. (figuratively) a task or service. KJV: burden.

φορτοσ.def: from φέρω (G5342); something carried, i.e. the cargo of a ship. KJV: lading.

φορτουνατοσ.def: of Latin origin; "fortunate"; Fortunatus, a Christian. KJV: Fortunatus.

φραγελλιον.def: neuter of a derivative from the base of φραγελλόω (G5417); a whip, i.e. Roman lash as a public punishment. KJV: scourge.

φραγελλοω.def: from a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum; to whip, i.e. lash as a public punishment. KJV: scourge.

φραγμοσ.def: from φράσσω (G5420); a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or figuratively). KJV: hedge (+ round about), partition.

φραζω.def: probably akin to φράσσω (G5420) through the idea of defining; to indicate (by word or act), i.e. (specially), to expound. KJV: declare.

φρασσω.def: apparently a strengthening form of the base of φρήν (G5424); to fence or inclose, i.e. (specially), to block up (figuratively, to silence). KJV: stop.

φρεαρ.def: of uncertain derivation; a hole in the ground (dug for obtaining or holding water or other purposes), i.e. a cistern or well; figuratively, an abyss (as a prison). KJV: well, pit.

φρεναπαταω.def: from φρεναπάτης (G5423); to be a mind-misleader, i.e. delude. KJV: deceive.

φρεναπατησ.def: from φρήν (G5424) and ἀπάτη (G539); a mind-misleader, i.e. seducer. KJV: deceiver.

φρην.def: probably from an obsolete φράω (to rein in or curb; compare φράσσω (G5420)); the midrif (as a partition of the body), i.e. (figuratively and by implication, of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by extension (also in the plural) the mind or cognitive faculties). KJV: understanding.

φρισσω.def: apparently a primary verb; to "bristle" or chill, i.e. shudder (fear). KJV: tremble.

φρονεω.def: from φρήν (G5424); to exercise the mind, i.e. entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience). KJV: set the affection on, (be) care(-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed), regard, savour, think.

φρονημα.def: from φρονέω (G5426); (mental) inclination or purpose. KJV: (be, + be carnally, + be spiritually) mind(-ed).

φρονησισ.def: from φρονέω (G5426); mental action or activity, i.e. intellectual or moral insight. KJV: prudence, wisdom.

φρονιμοσ.def: from φρήν (G5424); thoughtful, i.e. sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious character; while σοφός (G4680) denotes practical skill or acumen; and συνετός (G4908) indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense conceited (also in the comparative). KJV: wise(-r).

φρονιμωσ.def: adverb from φρόνιμος (G5429); prudently. KJV: wisely.

φροντιζω.def: from a derivative of φρήν (G5424); to exercise thought, i.e. be anxious. KJV: be careful.

φρουρεω.def: from a compound of πρό (G4253) and ὁράω (G3708); to be a watcher in advance, i.e. to mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect. KJV: keep (with a garrison).

φρυασσω.def: akin to βρύω (G1032), βρύχω (G1031); to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult. KJV: rage.

φρυγανον.def: neuter of a presumed derivative of φρύγω (to roast or parch; akin to the base of φλόξ (G5395)); something desiccated, i.e. a dry twig. KJV: stick.

φρυγια.def: probably of foreign origin; Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor. KJV: Phrygia.

φυγελλοσ.def: probably from φεύγω (G5343); fugitive; Phygellus, an apostate Christian. KJV: Phygellus.

φυγη.def: from φεύγω (G5343); a fleeing, i.e. escape. KJV: flight.

φυλακη.def: from φυλάσσω (G5442); a guarding or (concretely, guard), the act, the person; figuratively, the place, the condition, or (specially), the time (as a division of day or night), literally or figuratively. KJV: cage, hold, (im-)prison(-ment), ward, watch.

φυλακιζω.def: from φύλαξ (G5441); to incarcerate. KJV: imprison.

φυλακτηριον.def: neuter of a derivative of φυλάσσω (G5442); a guard-case, i.e. "phylactery" for wearing slips of Scripture texts. KJV: phylactery.

φυλαξ.def: from φυλάσσω (G5442); a watcher or sentry. KJV: keeper.

φυλασσω.def: probably from φυλή (G5443) through the idea of isolation; to watch, i.e. be on guard (literally of figuratively); by implication, to preserve, obey, avoid. KJV: beward, keep (self), observe, save.

φυλη.def: from φύω (G5453) (compare φύλλον (G5444)); an offshoot, i.e. race or clan. KJV: kindred, tribe.

φυλλον.def: from the same as φυλή (G5443); a sprout, i.e. leaf. KJV: leaf.

φυραμα.def: from a prolonged form of φύρω (to mix a liquid with a solid; perhaps akin to φύω (G5453) through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough. KJV: lump.

φυσικοσ.def: from φύσις (G5449); "physical", i.e. (by implication) instinctive. KJV: natural.

φυσικωσ.def: adverb from φυσικός (G5446); "physically", i.e. (by implication) instinctively. KJV: naturally.

φυσιοω.def: from φύσις (G5449) in the primary sense of blowing; to inflate, i.e. (figuratively) make proud (haughty). KJV: puff up.

φυσισ.def: from φύω (G5453); growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage. KJV: (man-)kind, nature(-al).

φυσιωσισ.def: from φυσιόω (G5448); inflation, i.e. (figuratively) haughtiness. KJV: swelling.

φυτεια.def: from φυτεύω (G5452); trans-planting, i.e. (concretely) a shrub or vegetable. KJV: plant.

φυτευω.def: from a derivative of φύω (G5453); to set out in the earth, i.e. implant; figuratively, to instil doctrine. KJV: plant.

φυω.def: a primary verb; probably originally, to "puff" or blow, i.e. to swell up; but only used in the implied sense, to germinate or grow (sprout, produce), literally or figuratively. KJV: spring (up).

φωλεοσ.def: of uncertain derivative; a burrow or lurking-place. KJV: hole.

φωνεω.def: from φωνή (G5456); to emit a sound (animal, human or instrumental); by implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation. KJV: call (for), crow, cry.

φωνη.def: probably akin to φαίνω (G5316) through the idea of disclosure; a tone (articulate, bestial or artificial); by implication, an address (for any purpose), saying or language. KJV: noise, sound, voice.

φωσ.def: from an obsolete φάω (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays; compare φαίνω (G5316), φημί (G5346)); luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative). KJV: fire, light.

φωστηρ.def: from φῶς (G5457); an illuminator, i.e. (concretely) a luminary, or (abstractly) brilliancy. KJV: light.

φωσφοροσ.def: from φῶς (G5457) and φέρω (G5342); light-bearing ("phosphorus"), i.e. (specially), the morning-star (figuratively). KJV: day star.

φωτεινοσ.def: from φῶς (G5457); lustrous, i.e. transparent or well-illuminated (figuratively). KJV: bright, full of light.

φωτιζω.def: from φῶς (G5457); to shed rays, i.e. to shine or (transitively) to brighten up (literally or figuratively). KJV: enlighten, illuminate, (bring to, give) light, make to see.
